newsitem.title: MEXICO: Amresco wins Mexico bank asset auction.
newsitem.headline: Amresco wins Mexico bank asset auction.

text.p: Mexico's VVA said on Wednesday U.S. financial services company Amresco Inc's Amresco Financial LP affiliate had won the first auction of Mexican bank assets worth 135 million pesos ($17.1 million).
"The winning bidder of the auction was Amresco Financial LP, which paid 66.8 million pesos ($8.5 million), thereby acquiring the whole of the portfolio," VVA said in a statement.
Mexico's Valuation and Sale of Assets (VVA) is a government agency charged with selling assets taken over by Mexico's FOBAPROA bank bail-out fund after the 1994-95 financial crisis.

VVA said 13 groups took part in Wednesday's auction, jointly lead managed by Bankers Trust and Mexican brokerage GBM, which was the first in a series designed to recover the value of bank assets after creditors failed to keep up payments.
"The price reflects the fact that two-thirds of the portfolio were credits denominated in UDIs (inflation indexed investment units)," the statement said.

VVA had originally said that the first portfolio of assets up for auction would total 150 million pesos ($19 million). But one debtor paid 15 million pesos ($1.9 million) owed to its bank in an eleventh hour self-rescue effort, reducing the auction total to 135 million pesos.
